cues.text: And your hand is already on your phone.
You didn't decide that. So who did?
It's a mind that can't lock onto anything.
Attention keeps searching for something to hold. And that feels bad.
Your brain has learned a shortcut.
It's relief. The discomfort fades, for a moment.
And every time relief follows the reach, the shortcut gets a little easier to take.
That's why you keep scrolling after it stopped being fun.
Wanting and liking run on different circuits. One can grow while the other fades.
The urge to reach isn't a sign you enjoy it. It's a sign you've learned it.
Next time, notice the cue. And wait ten seconds.
The loop can't run without the response.
